title: Compressing Streaming Neural Audio Encoders via Latent-Space Distillation
gist: Apple researchers compress the always-on speech tokenizer that feeds on-device Dictation audio into Apple's sparsely activated foundation model by distilling on the pre-quantizer latent rather than tokens or output distributions. At 2.8x compression the student stays within 1.9% relative WER of its teacher on five of six pairs with no fine-tuning, and beats an equal-size independently trained tokenizer by 3.9% relative, reflecting DRAM contention as the binding constraint for on-device AI.

insights.claim: Apple's system-wide Dictation runs entirely on-device, with speech reaching the on-device foundation model through an audio tokenizer (encoder) that maps short waveform windows into the representation the language model reads.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Confirms Apple's architecture routes voice input into an on-device LLM, making on-device speech a direct consumer of device memory and compute budgets.
insights.quote: System-wide Dictation on Apple devices runs entirely on-device

insights.claim: Apple's on-device foundation model is sparsely activated under Instruction-Following Pruning, so only a small subset of its experts sits in DRAM at any time, and the always-on speech tokenizer competes for that same DRAM.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: DRAM capacity, not raw compute, is the binding constraint for Apple's on-device AI; watch device memory configurations and memory suppliers as a lever on feature scope.
insights.quote: only a small subset of its experts occupies DRAM at any time, so the always-on tokenizer competes for the same memory

insights.claim: For an always-on on-device speech tokenizer, parameter count bears directly on power consumption and latency, making encoder compression a first-order product lever rather than an academic optimization.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Model-compression advances translate into battery life and responsiveness, a key differentiator for edge AI versus cloud-dependent assistants.
insights.quote: its parameter count bears directly on power and latency

insights.claim: Apple compresses its speech tokenizer by distilling on the pre-quantizer latent that the language model actually consumes, rather than on discrete tokens or the output distribution, since that latent is the last representation shared by both token interfaces.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Choosing the supervision target at the shared interface is a general recipe for shrinking multimodal front-ends feeding LLMs on edge devices.
insights.quote: taking as the supervision target neither the discrete token nor the output distribution but the pre-quantizer latent the model actually consumes

insights.claim: The distillation recipe trains only the student encoder to regress the teacher's per-frame latent with a squared-error loss, using a single affine layer to absorb the teacher-student width mismatch.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: A simple, cheap training recipe lowers the cost of producing smaller on-device models, favoring fast iteration across device tiers.
insights.locator: We train only the student encoder

insights.claim: Because the distillation target sits before both the quantizer and the language-model bridge, one recipe covers both supported token interfaces and works for tokenizers pretrained alone or jointly trained with a language model.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Reusability across interfaces and training regimes suggests Apple can standardize compression across its speech stack instead of bespoke per-model work.
insights.quote: one recipe covers both token interfaces we support

insights.claim: At 2.8x compression, the distilled speech-tokenizer student stays within 1.9% relative word error rate of its teacher on five of six teacher-student pairs without any fine-tuning.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Near-3x smaller always-on audio encoders at minimal accuracy cost frees DRAM for more LLM experts or features on existing hardware.

insights.claim: A latent-distilled speech tokenizer outperforms an independently trained tokenizer of identical capacity by 3.9% relative WER, showing distillation beats training small models from scratch.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Supports the view that large teacher models remain valuable even for edge deployment, since their quality transfers into cheaper student models.
insights.quote: improves on an independently trained tokenizer of identical capacity by 3.9% relative

insights.claim: Two authors of the Apple speech-tokenizer distillation paper are marked as having done the work while at Apple, with current affiliations listed as NVIDIA and Anthropic respectively.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Signals ongoing outflow of Apple on-device ML talent to AI leaders, a soft indicator worth tracking for Apple's AI execution.
insights.locator: † NVIDIA§ Anthropic** Work done while at Apple
